order: Fix every finding from the prior review round in full. Replace the copied-over runner semantics in the research seat's brief with the execution tool's real behavior: live working tree, no sandbox pinning, no automatic retries, exactly one call per order, with unavailability escalated to the coordinating role. Make the reconciliation between the write-capable runner and the read-only plan explicit and mechanical across the research, analysis, and archiving briefs — every order must carry the read-only constraint in its own text and must also pass the forbid parameter, described only as a brief-level prohibition instruction, never as a sandboxed block. Rewrite the earlier incident narrative to the evidence-supported account, withdrawing the unsupported claim entirely rather than softening it, and correct two exercise reports whose dispatch-time details were dropped or wrong. Clear the minor findings too: stale status rows, a wrong tool count, an unjustified omission, an unexplained repeated log line, and a misattributed casting rule.
claims: We resolved all four major findings and the follow-on minors from the prior round across exactly ten files (169 insertions, 46 deletions): the runner-semantics rewrite, the read-only reconciliation across three briefs, the incident-narrative rewrite, and two corrected exercise reports. The tool count was fixed to the actual four registered tools, confirmed by checking each brief against the tool registry. Each change was verified line by line against the source file it corrects.
